title: Pots and pans
hookLine: Brother Lawrence, a Carmelite cook, turning an omelette for the love of God

lines: A CLUMSY COOK AT THE STOVE.
THE PRACTICE OF THE PRESENCE OF GOD.
cards: A monastery kitchen in Paris. Steam, noise, people calling for things all at once.
At the stove stands a lay brother of the Carmelites, a former soldier, by his own account clumsy, who says he had a great dislike for kitchen work.
His name in religion is Brother Lawrence of the Resurrection, and you first met him at this stove on day two hundred seventy-eight.
He left no big book: some letters, and a visiting priest's notes of their conversations, published after his death and known in English by a title that stuck, The Practice of the Presence of God.

teach.h: TURN THE CAKE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD.
teach.b: Lawrence's secret, as he told it, was almost embarrassingly simple. He would turn the little cake frying in the pan for the love of God.
When it was done, if there was nothing else to do, he'd bow down and thank God, and then get up again, happier than a king. He'd pick a piece of straw off the ground, for the love of God.
The task didn't matter; what mattered was who he did it for.

teach.h: WORK TIME, PRAYER TIME, THE SAME.
teach.b: He said that for him the time of work didn't differ from the time of prayer.
In the noise and clatter of his kitchen, with several people calling for different things, he said he had God as calmly as if he were on his knees before the sacrament.

teach.h: WANDER OFF, COME BACK, NO DRAMA.
teach.b: That's the whole teaching: not a technique, but a habit of turning toward God in the middle of things, and turning back whenever you notice you've wandered off. He wasn't hard on himself about the wandering.
When he forgot, he admitted it, and came back.

teach.h: WHATSOEVER YE DO, AS TO THE LORD.
teach.b: Paul had said it long before: "And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men." And again: "whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God."
Lawrence just took Paul at his word, in a kitchen. Two days ago it was John's mountain of nothing; yesterday, his flame. Lawrence belongs to the same family, and he brings it down to the stove.
The holy place, for him, was wherever his hands were.

how: Christians across churches read Brother Lawrence's The Practice of the Presence of God and try to keep a simple awareness of God through ordinary work, turning back to God briefly and often during the day.

games.q: you're Brother Lawrence. the kitchen is loud, three people want things at once, and your mind has wandered far from God. what do you do?
o: leave the kitchen to go pray in the chapel.
quietly turn back to God, right there at the stove.
scold yourself for being a bad monk.
games.why: Lawrence said the time of work didn't differ from the time of prayer. when he wandered, he simply came back, in the middle of the noise.

practice: Think of the next ordinary thing your hands will do, making coffee, a sandwich, folding a towel, washing a pan, and picture doing it slowly, all the way through.
Then decide who it's for: if you pray, the love of God, the way Lawrence turned his cake; if you don't, someone you love, or simply full attention. Let the plain task be enough.

wordCard.voice: Pots and pans. Brother Lawrence's kitchen, where turning a cake for the love of God was as much prayer as kneeling in church.

carryVoice: Your line: turn it for love. Wandering off and coming back is part of it. I'll be here tomorrow.
